def factor_volume_price_beta_liquidity_adaptive(df):
    """Volume-price coupling beta with adaptive illiquidity attenuation."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret_1 = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    vol_chg = df_copy["volume"].pct_change()
    cov = ret_1.rolling(20, min_periods=5).cov(vol_chg)
    var = vol_chg.rolling(20, min_periods=5).var()
    beta = cov / var.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    beta = beta.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    dollar_volume = df_copy["volume"] * df_copy["close"]
    illiquidity = (df_copy["high"] - df_copy["low"]) / dollar_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    avg_illiquidity = illiquidity.rolling(10, min_periods=5).mean()
    weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + avg_illiquidity)
    factor = beta * weight
    df_copy["factor_volume_price_beta_liquidity_adaptive"] = factor
    return df_copy["factor_volume_price_beta_liquidity_adaptive"]
description: Primary mechanism from parent alpha-composite-0002: rolling beta of return on volume change captures informed flow (positive beta) versus divergence (negative beta). Lightweight modifier borrowed from parent g1_crossover_alpha_composite_0002_alpha_liquidity_gen0_0001_83bffab0: Amihud-style illiquidity attenuation scales down the beta signal when average illiquidity is high. To make the attenuation more responsive to current liquidity conditions, the illiquidity lookback is shortened to 10 days while keeping the beta window at 20. This preserves the raw volume-price coupling structure and payoff profile, targeting improved IC/ICIR by reducing noise from stale liquidity estimates. No cross-sectional transform is applied because both parents demonstrated strong RankICIR and payoff evidence from the raw mechanism.
